question: What is the purpose of the registration tracking flag in the schematic collection class that prevents setup methods from being called after the schematic has been registered once?
answer:
# Purpose of `_got_registered_once` Flag in Schematic

The `_got_registered_once` flag in the `Schematic` class prevents setup methods from being called after the schematic has been registered, ensuring **consistency across multiple registrations**.

## How It Works

When `Schematic.enroll` is called (during `app.enroll_plan`), it sets `self._got_registered_once = True`. After that point, any `@preparationmethod`-decorated setup method (routes, record callbacks, hook decorators) will raise an `AssertionError` when called.

**Source:** `src/quill/sansio/schematics.py:L213-221`

```python
def _verify_configuration_completed(self, f_name: str) -> None:
    if self._got_registered_once:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"The setup method '{f_name}' can no longer be called on the schematic"
            f" '{self.name}'. It has already been registered at least once, any"
            " changes will not be applied consistently.\n"
            "Make sure all imports, decorators, functions, etc. needed to set up"
            " the schematic are done before registering it."
        )
```

## The Core Problem It Prevents

If you registered a schematic with `app.enroll_plan`, then added new routes to it, those routes would **not** be registered on the application. This inconsistency—where some registrations have the new routes and others don't—is what the flag prevents.

The `preparationmethod` decorator (`src/quill/sansio/skeleton.py:L42-49`) wraps every setup method to call `_verify_configuration_completed` before execution, enforcing this guarantee across all setup methods including `route`, `record`, and hook decorators.
